queries.text: Which documented Muninn design boundaries govern durable memory operations, owner scope, optional processing, and retrieval behavior?

candidates.text: Muninn can create an explicit, property-free link from a preference to an entity. The operation is idempotent and does not add a separate read path or bridge operation.
Entity enrichment and location geocoding are opt-in. Without explicit configuration the provider is not reachable, and existing calls and stored data remain unchanged.
Entity deduplication is disabled by default. Explicit request flags enable the documented single-entity resolution policy.
Message extraction is an opt-in local processing stage. Configuring an adapter alone does not change existing message ingestion.
The long-term surface distinguishes global graph entities and facts from owner-scoped preferences. Caller-supplied owner identifiers define data scope, not authentication.
Conversation identity uses owner scope and session identity. Reads, listings, searches, and deletions require scope, and UUIDs do not bypass that boundary.
Preference retrieval combines supplied filters with AND. The documented filters cover active state, entity linkage, and validity time.
Schema initialization uses versioned migrations and coordination. The documented setup path does not run inference or depend on embedding-provider identity.
Muninn documents a local CPU/F32 MiniLM provider as a candidate with explicit configuration. The document distinguishes implementation status from acceptance.
The pinned reference and compatibility boundaries are recorded separately from claims about implemented behavior; the reference lock identifies baseline inputs and known gaps.
